title: The Psychology of Cognitive Biases in Decision Making
subtitle: Boğaziçi BUEPT Tarzı Note-Taking Sınavı
instructions_tr: Bu bir Note-Taking (Not Alma) sınavıdır. Dinleme esnasında sorular gizlidir. Aşağıdaki dijital not defterine önemli kavramları, neden-sonuç ilişkilerini ve örnekleri not alınız. Dinleme bittikten sonra 'Soruları Aç' butonuna basarak notlarınıza bakıp soruları yanıtlayınız.
audio_script: Good morning class. Today we will examine how unconscious mental shortcuts, known in cognitive psychology as cognitive biases, systematically distort human rationality. Although human beings pride themselves on being logical decision-makers, empirical evidence demonstrates that our cognitive faculties rely heavily on heuristics. Two of the most pervasive biases are confirmation bias and the framing effect. First, let us look at confirmation bias. Confirmation bias is the tendency of individuals to search for, interpret, and recall information in a manner that validates their preexisting beliefs, while simultaneously disregarding contrary evidence. In an academic experiment conducted by Peter Wason in nineteen sixty, subjects consistently tested hypotheses by seeking confirming instances rather than attempting to falsify their assumptions. In contemporary digital society, algorithms on social media platforms amplify confirmation bias, creating ideological echo chambers where divergent opinions are systematically excluded. Now, let us shift our attention to the second phenomenon: the framing effect. Pioneered by psychologists Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky in nineteen eighty-one, the framing effect demonstrates that people react differently to a particular choice depending on whether it is presented as a gain or as a loss. For example, when medical patients are informed that a surgical procedure has a ninety percent survival rate, an overwhelming majority consent to the operation. Conversely, when the identical statistical reality is framed as having a ten percent mortality rate, acceptance rates decline precipitously. Thus, the psychological architecture of human perception reveals that risk aversion is context-dependent. To conclude, awareness of these cognitive vulnerabilities is essential for objective critical thinking, scientific inquiry, and sound public policy. In our next lecture, we will examine debiasing techniques.
suggested_notes_tr: Ana Tema: Bilişsel Çarpıtmalar (Cognitive Biases) ve Akılcılık
1. Confirmation Bias (Doğrulama Yanlılığı): Var olan inançları destekleyen bilgileri arayıp tersini yok sayma. Peter Wason (1960) deneyi. Sosyal medya yankı odaları.
2. Framing Effect (Çerçeveleme Etkisi): Kahneman & Tversky (1981). Bilginin sunuluş biçimi kararı değiştirir. %90 hayatta kalma vs %10 ölüm oranı örneği.
Sonuç: Eleştirel düşünme için bu önyargıların farkında olmak şarttır.

options.text: Individuals actively seek to falsify their preconceived assumptions.
Subjects prioritize seeking confirming evidence over attempting to disconfirm hypotheses.

Social media algorithms have reduced the impact of confirmation bias.

questions.explanation_tr: Derste belirtildiği üzere Wason'ın 1960 yılındaki deneyi, insanların hipotezlerini yanlışlamaya (falsify) çalışmak yerine doğrulamaya yönelik kanıt aradıklarını (confirming instances) göstermiştir.

options.text: Choices are evaluated based on how outcomes are framed as gains or losses.
Patients consistently prefer riskier medical procedures regardless of wording.

Risk tolerance increases when negative outcomes are emphasized.

questions.explanation_tr: Kahneman ve Tversky'nin Çerçeveleme Etkisi (Framing Effect) teorisine göre, kararlar seçeneğin bir kazanç (gain) mı yoksa kayıp (loss) olarak mı sunulduğuna bağlı olarak tamamen değişir.

options.text: To suggest that algorithms encourage diverse perspectives.

questions.explanation_tr: Konuşmacı, sosyal medya algoritmalarının ideolojik 'yankı odaları' (echo chambers) yaratarak doğrulama yanlılığını pekiştirdiğini ve farklı görüşleri dışladığını vurgulamak için sosyal medyadan bahsetmiştir.

title: Smart Electrical Grids and Renewable Energy Integration
subtitle: İTÜ Proficiency Tarzı While-Listening Sınavı
instructions_tr: Bu bir While-Listening (Dinlerken Cevaplama) sınavıdır. Sorular ses kaydı boyunca açıktır. Kaydı dinlerken eş zamanlı olarak soruları yanıtlayabilirsiniz.
audio_script: Good afternoon prospective engineers. Today, modern electrical engineering is undergoing a fundamental transformation. For over a century, traditional electrical grids operated on a unidirectional flow model: centralized power plants generated electricity from fossil fuels and transmitted it down to passive consumers. However, the rapid proliferation of renewable energy sources, specifically solar photovoltaic systems and offshore wind farms, has rendered this conventional architecture obsolete. Renewable power generation is inherently intermittent and decentralized. Wind patterns fluctuate unpredictably, and solar irradiance ceases during nocturnal hours. To resolve this imbalance between fluctuating supply and volatile demand, engineers have developed the concept of the Smart Grid. A smart grid utilizes bi-directional digital communication networks, advanced metering infrastructure, and automated sensors to dynamically balance load distributions. Furthermore, utility-scale battery energy storage systems, such as lithium-ion and flow batteries, play a pivotal role in frequency regulation. In conclusion, the transition toward carbon neutrality requires not merely green generation, but intelligent transmission systems.

Yenilenebilir Sorunu: Kesintili (intermittent) üretim ve merkezi olmayan yapı.
Akıllı Şebeke (Smart Grid): Çift yönlü iletişim, anlık yük dengeleme.
Depolama: Batarya sistemleri frekans regülasyonu sağlar.

Through automated smart meters installed at consumer homes.

title: Bioclimatic Urban Architecture and Heat Island Mitigation
subtitle: ODTÜ EPE Tarzı Note-Taking Sınavı
instructions_tr: ODTÜ EPE formatında not alma simülasyonu. Ses kaydını dinlerken notlarınızı alınız. Kayıt bitiminde sorular açılacak ve cevaplayacaksınız.
audio_script: Welcome students. In today's architectural seminar, we shall investigate bioclimatic architecture as a mitigation strategy against the Urban Heat Island effect. As metropolitan areas expand, impermeable surfaces such as asphalt roads and concrete high-rises absorb solar radiation, releasing thermal energy overnight. Consequently, urban centers frequently experience ambient temperatures three to seven degrees Celsius higher than neighboring rural districts. Bioclimatic architecture tackles this predicament through three fundamental design interventions: passive natural ventilation corridors, green infrastructure roofs, and albedo optimization. Albedo refers to the fraction of solar radiation reflected by a surface. By substituting dark asphalt with high-albedo reflective coatings and permeable pavers, surface heat absorption is reduced by up to forty percent. Concurrently, green roofs laden with drought-resistant vegetation reduce urban stormwater runoff while facilitating evaporative cooling. Ultimately, sustainable urban design requires synchronizing architectural geometry with microclimatic wind patterns.
suggested_notes_tr: Sorun: Urban Heat Island (UHI) - Beton/asfalt ısınması, 3-7°C daha sıcak şehir merkezleri.
Çözüm: Biyoklimatik Mimari (3 müdahale):
1. Doğal havalandırma koridorları (passive ventilation).
2. Yeşil çatılar (green roofs): Su tutma ve evaporative cooling.
3. Albedo optimizasyonu: Güneş ışığını yansıtma yüzdesi. Açık renk kaplamalarla %40 ısı azalması.

Because wind currents are entirely absent in rural districts.

options.text: The speed of subterranean stormwater runoff.
The structural load capacity of concrete columns.
The percentage of solar radiation reflected by a surface material.
The rate at which vegetation produces oxygen during daylight.

questions.explanation_tr: Albedo, bir yüzeyin üzerine düşen güneş radyasyonunu yansıtma (reflect) oranıdır.

options.text: Up to ten percent.
Up to twenty-five percent.
Up to forty percent.
Nearly eighty percent.

questions.explanation_tr: Konuşmacı 'surface heat absorption is reduced by up to forty percent' demiştir.

options.text: Increasing asphalt durability and decreasing rural temperatures.
Reducing stormwater runoff and facilitating evaporative cooling.

questions.explanation_tr: Yeşil çatılar yağmur suyu akışını azaltır (reduce stormwater runoff) ve buharlaşma yoluyla serinletme (evaporative cooling) sağlar.

title: The Ethical Implications of Autonomous Medical AI
subtitle: Bilkent COPE Tarzı While-Listening Sınavı
instructions_tr: Bu bir While-Listening (Dinlerken Cevaplama) sınavıdır. Ses kaydı çalarken soruları eş zamanlı okuyup doğru seçenekleri işaretleyiniz.
audio_script: Welcome to today's bioethics colloquium. Over the past decade, deep learning convolutional neural networks have surpassed human dermatologists and radiologists in detecting early-stage melanomas and lung nodules. However, transitioning these diagnostic algorithms from controlled clinical benchmarks to emergency triage presents profound ethical and legal quandaries. The principal conundrum is algorithmic opacity, colloquially referred to by computer scientists as the black-box dilemma. Deep neural networks evaluate millions of non-linear parameter weights; consequently, even the computer software engineers who architected the models cannot provide a human-interpretable clinical rationale for why a particular diagnostic recommendation was generated. Under European data privacy regulations and medical malpractice tort laws, patients possess an explicit right to an explanation. If an autonomous algorithm misdiagnoses a malignant tumor or mistakenly triages an urgent cardiac case, who bears legal liability: the attending physician who followed the software, the software vendor who trained the model, or the hospital administration that procured the technology? In our upcoming seminar, we will dissect the emerging legal frameworks of algorithmic accountability.

Başarı: Erken evre kanser ve melanom tespitinde uzman doktorları geçmesi.
Temel Sorun 1: Black-Box Dilemma (Algoritmik opaklık - kararın neden verildiğinin açıklanamaması).
Temel Sorun 2: Yasal Sorumluluk (Hatalı teşhiste hekim mi, yazılımcı mı, hastane mi sorumlu?).

options.text: The physical overheating of hospital computer server hardware.
The inability of engineers to provide a human-interpretable rationale for algorithm outputs.
The complete prohibition of artificial intelligence software in European hospitals.
The failure of convolutional networks to detect melanoma cells accurately.

questions.explanation_tr: Metinde kara kutu (black-box) sorunu; derin sinir ağlarının milyonlarca parametreyi değerlendirmesi sebebiyle mühendislerin bile algoritmanın verdiği teşhis kararının klinik gerekçesini insan anlayışına uygun açıklayamaması olarak ifade edilmiştir.

options.text: The right to inspect the source code of hospital software.

title: Epigenetics, Neuroplasticity, and Cognitive Aging
subtitle: Boğaziçi BUEPT Tarzı Note-Taking Sınavı
instructions_tr: Bu bir Note-Taking (Not Alma) sınavıdır. Dinleme esnasında sorular gizlidir. Aşağıdaki dijital not defterine dersin ana fikrini, bilimsel terimleri, epigenetik mekanizmaları ve örnekleri not alınız. Dinleme bittikten sonra 'Soruları Aç' butonuna basarak notlarınıza bakıp soruları yanıtlayınız.
audio_script: Good morning, colleagues. Today, we will examine one of the most transformative paradigm shifts in modern neuroscience: the convergence of epigenetics and neuroplasticity in the context of cognitive aging. Historically, neurobiology operated under a deterministic dogma: that our genetic code represented an unalterable blueprint, and that the adult human brain was structurally immutable, condemned to gradual neuronal depletion. Contemporary empirical research has dismantled both assumptions. First, epigenetics reveals that while our underlying nucleotide sequence remains static, gene expression is dynamically modulated by environmental interactions. Molecular mechanisms—predominantly DNA methylation and histone acetylation—act as biochemical switches, silencing or activating specific genes in response to chronic stress, nutritional patterns, and cognitive stimulation. Concurrently, neuroplasticity demonstrates that adult neural circuits retain lifelong structural flexibility. Even in senescence, the hippocampus can generate new neurons—a process known as adult neurogenesis—and forge novel synaptic arborizations. This dynamic capacity underpins the concept of 'cognitive reserve.' Individuals who routinely engage in rigorous intellectual inquiry, multilingualism, and aerobic exercise accumulate dense synaptic redundancies. Consequently, when pathological markers such as beta-amyloid plaques emerge, resilient brains reorganize compensatory networks, delaying clinical manifestations of dementia for years. Ultimately, human cognitive longevity is neither genetically predetermined nor fatalistically destined to decay. Through intentional lifestyle modifications, we exert substantial regulatory agency over the molecular architecture of our own minds. In our next session, we will examine pharmacological epigenetic modulators.
suggested_notes_tr: Ana Tema: Nörobiyolojide Paradigma Değişimi - Genetik kadercilik ve sabit beyin anlayışının yıkılması.
Epigenetik Mekanizmalar: DNA nükleotid dizilimi değişmez, ancak DNA metilasyonu ve histon asetilasyonu ile gen ifadesi açılıp kapanır.
Nöroplastisite ve Nörogenez: Yaşlılıkta (senescence) dahi hipokampusta yeni nöron oluşumu ve sinaptik dallanmalar mümkündür.
Bilişsel Rezerv (Cognitive Reserve): Zihinsel uğraş ve egzersiz sinaptik yedeklilik sağlar; beta-amiloid plaklara karşı telafi edici ağlar kurarak demansı geciktirir.
Sonuç / Çıkarım: Bilişsel yaşlanma kaçınılmaz bir çöküş değildir; yaşam tarzı tercihleriyle beyin mimarisi üzerinde düzenleyici kontrol (regulatory agency) kurulabilir.

questions.question: What is the central paradigm shift in modern neuroscience highlighted by the lecturer?

options.text: The definitive proof that cognitive aging is strictly dictated by inherited nucleotide sequences.
The transition from genetic and structural determinism to dynamic gene-environment and neural plasticity models.
The discovery that pharmacological modulators can completely replace lifestyle modifications in dementia care.

questions.explanation_tr: Dersin ana teması, geleneksel nörobiyolojinin 'genetik kodun değiştirilemez bir yazgı olduğu ve yetişkin beyninin sabit kaldığı' yönündeki determinist dogmasının yıkılmasıdır. Konuşmacı, epigenetik (dinamik gen-çevre etkileşimi) ve nöroplastisite (ömür boyu süren beyin esnekliği) sayesinde insan beyninin dinamik olarak yeniden yapılandığını vurgulamaktadır.

questions.question: According to the lecture, how do molecular mechanisms like DNA methylation and histone acetylation affect genes?

options.text: They permanently alter the fundamental nucleotide sequence of the organism's DNA.
They eradicate beta-amyloid plaques before any synaptic damage can occur in the hippocampus.
They act as biochemical switches that modulate gene expression without changing the genetic code itself.
They prevent the hippocampus from undergoing adult neurogenesis under chronic stress.

questions.explanation_tr: Konuşmacı açıkça epigenetik mekanizmaların (DNA metilasyonu ve histon asetilasyonu) altta yatan nükleotid dizilimini değiştirmeden ('underlying nucleotide sequence remains static'), gen ifadesini biyokimyasal anahtarlar gibi açıp kapattığını ('biochemical switches, silencing or activating specific genes') ifade etmiştir.

questions.question: What enables individuals with high cognitive reserve to delay the clinical symptoms of dementia?

options.text: Their brains establish redundant synaptic connections and recruit compensatory neural networks.
Their genetic profiles eliminate the physical formation of toxic beta-amyloid plaques.
They avoid all metabolic and physical stressors throughout their adult lifespan.
They rely exclusively on synthetic epigenetic drugs to halt natural cellular senescence.

questions.explanation_tr: Metne göre zihinsel olarak aktif bireyler sinaptik yedeklilik (dense synaptic redundancies) biriktirir. Beyinde beta-amiloid plakları oluşsa bile, dirençli beyinler telafi edici ağları (compensatory networks) devreye sokarak klinik demans semptomlarının ortaya çıkmasını yıllarca geciktirir.

questions.question: Which statement best captures the speaker's stance regarding the trajectory of human cognitive aging?

options.text: Intellectual decline is an unavoidable biological fate that renders lifestyle choices inconsequential.
Proactive lifestyle modifications grant individuals meaningful regulatory influence over brain health.

Adult neurogenesis is a laboratory artifact with negligible relevance to real-world neural preservation.

questions.explanation_tr: Konuşmacı sonuç bölümünde bilişsel uzun ömürlülüğün genetik olarak önceden belirlenmediğini ('neither genetically predetermined nor fatalistically destined to decay'), bilinçli yaşam tarzı seçimleriyle zihnimizin moleküler mimarisi üzerinde önemli bir düzenleme gücüne ('substantial regulatory agency') sahip olduğumuzu savunmaktadır.

title: Behavioral Economics and Choice Architecture in Public Policy
subtitle: Bilkent COPE Tarzı While-Listening Sınavı
instructions_tr: Bu bir While-Listening (Dinlerken Cevaplama) sınavıdır. Ses kaydı çalarken soruları eş zamanlı okuyup doğru seçenekleri işaretleyiniz.
audio_script: Good afternoon, class. Today, we will explore how behavioral economics has reshaped modern public policy through the concept of choice architecture. For decades, neoclassical economic theory operated on the premise of 'Homo economicus'—the assumption that human agents are perfectly rational actors who consistently calculate costs and benefits to maximize personal utility. However, empirical behavioral research led by scholars like Richard Thaler and Cass Sunstein proved that actual decision-makers exhibit bounded rationality. Real people rely on cognitive shortcuts, suffer from inertia, and are disproportionately influenced by how options are organized. To address this reality without imposing restrictive mandates or financial penalties, governments increasingly utilize 'nudges.' A nudge subtly alters the decision-making environment without forbidding any choices or altering economic incentives. The most potent tool in choice architecture is the default option. In classical opt-in systems—such as organ donation or supplemental pension schemes—citizens must actively complete paperwork to participate, resulting in participation rates often hovering below thirty percent. Conversely, when policymakers switch to an opt-out default—where enrollment is automatic but opting out remains entirely cost-free—participation frequently surges past ninety percent. This framework, termed 'libertarian paternalism,' preserves individual liberty while steering citizens toward beneficial welfare outcomes. Nonetheless, ethical critics raise legitimate concerns regarding transparency, questioning whether subtle psychological nudges border on covert paternalistic manipulation when citizens remain unaware of institutional influence.
suggested_notes_tr: Ana Tema: Davranışsal İktisat ve Kamu Politikasında Karar Mimarisi (Choice Architecture).
Klasik İktisat vs Davranışsal Gerçeklik: 'Homo economicus' (tam rasyonel insan) yanılgısına karşı sınırlı rasyonalite (bounded rationality) ve eylemsizlik (inertia).
Dürtme Teorisi (Nudge): Thaler & Sunstein - Seçenekleri yasaklamadan ve ekonomik teşvikleri değiştirmeden karar ortamını yeniden düzenleme.
En Etkili Araç - Varsayılan Seçenek (Default Option): Opt-in (%30 altı katılım) yerine otomatik katılımlı Opt-out sistemiyle katılımın %90'ın üzerine fırlaması.
Özgürlükçü Babacıllık (Libertarian Paternalism) ve Etik Tartışma: Bireysel özgürlüğü koruma iddiası ile şeffaflık eksikliği ve örtük manipülasyon (covert manipulation) eleştirisi.

questions.question: How does behavioral economics challenge the classical concept of 'Homo economicus'?

options.text: By showing that human agents operate with bounded rationality rather than flawless mathematical logic.
By demonstrating that economic incentives are completely irrelevant to human decision-making.
By proving that financial penalties are the only effective mechanism to modify consumer behavior.
By establishing that market consumers consistently calculate optimal long-term utility.

questions.explanation_tr: Konuşmacı klasik iktisadın 'insanların her zaman kusursuz rasyonel fayda maksimizasyonu yaptığı (Homo economicus)' varsayımına karşı, gerçek insanların sınırlı rasyonellik (bounded rationality), kestirme yollar ve eylemsizlik ile hareket ettiğini ortaya koymuştur.

questions.question: According to the lecturer, what distinguishes a 'nudge' from traditional regulatory interventions?

options.text: It enforces compulsory participation by imposing severe legal fines on non-compliant citizens.
It subtly alters the choice context without banning alternative options or changing financial costs.
It completely removes negative alternatives from the consumer's decision environment.
It requires citizens to pass economic literacy examinations before choosing.

questions.explanation_tr: Metinde dürtmenin (nudge) hiçbir seçeneği yasaklamadan ('without forbidding any choices') ve ekonomik teşvikleri/maliyetleri değiştirmeden ('altering economic incentives') karar alma ortamını incelikle değiştirdiği belirtilmiştir.

questions.question: What occurs when policymakers transition from an opt-in to an opt-out default system in pension or donation programs?

options.text: Citizen participation rates drop significantly due to heightened administrative paperwork.
The financial cost of administering public welfare programs triples immediately.
Participation rates frequently surge from under thirty percent to over ninety percent.
Citizens lose their fundamental legal right to withdraw from the government program.

questions.explanation_tr: Konuşmacı, klasik opt-in (onay vererek katılma) sisteminde katılımın %30'un altında kaldığını, ancak varsayılanın opt-out (otomatik dahil olup dilediğinde çıkabilme) yapılmasıyla katılım oranlarının sıklıkla %90'ın üzerine çıktığını ('surges past ninety percent') belirtmektedir.

questions.question: What primary ethical concern is raised by critics regarding the philosophy of 'libertarian paternalism'?

options.text: It fails to achieve any statistically measurable impact on public welfare outcomes.
It may cross the boundary into covert psychological manipulation when citizens lack transparency.
It forces private commercial enterprises to bear the full expense of policy reforms.
It restricts personal freedom of choice by outlawing unhealthy consumer products.

questions.explanation_tr: Metnin sonunda etik eleştirmenlerin şeffaflık konusuna dikkat çektiği ve vatandaşların kurumsal yönlendirmeden habersiz olduğu durumlarda bu ince psikolojik dürtmelerin örtük bir babacıl manipülasyona dönüşüp dönüşmediğini sorguladığı ('border on covert paternalistic manipulation') aktarılmıştır.

title: Circular Economy and Industrial Symbiosis in Resource-Constrained Economies
subtitle: ODTÜ EPE Tarzı Note-Taking Sınavı
instructions_tr: ODTÜ EPE formatında not alma simülasyonu. Ses kaydını dinlerken notlarınızı alınız. Kayıt bitiminde sorular açılacak ve notlarınıza dayanarak soruları cevaplayacaksınız.
audio_script: Good morning, engineering scholars. Today we examine industrial symbiosis as an operational foundation for the circular economy. Conventional manufacturing operates on a throughput-intensive linear model: virgin materials are extracted, processed, and ultimately discarded as non-recyclable refuse. Industrial symbiosis fundamentally disrupts this degenerative paradigm by organizing geographically clustered industries into closed-loop metabolic ecosystems. In such networks, the residual effluent, discarded by-product, or surplus thermal energy of one manufacturing facility is systematically repurposed as the direct secondary feedstock or energy supply for an adjacent enterprise. The quintessential empirical paradigm of this architecture is the Kalundborg eco-industrial park in Denmark. In Kalundborg, a large-scale combined heat and power plant pipelines high-temperature surplus steam directly to an adjacent pharmaceutical facility and an enzyme fermentation plant, eliminating independent industrial boiler combustion. Simultaneously, calcium sulfate dihydrate, commonly known as synthetic gypsum, is recovered directly from the sulfur dioxide flue-gas desulfurization scrubbers of the power station. This synthetic gypsum completely supplants virgin mined gypsum at an adjacent gypsum wallboard manufacturing plant. Cumulatively, these symbiotic exchanges conserve more than three million cubic meters of groundwater annually, achieve over six hundred thousand tons of net carbon dioxide abatement, and transform toxic disposal liabilities into lucrative commercial assets. audio_script: Good afternoon, class. In modern aerospace engineering, structural efficiency is fundamentally governed by material selection. For decades, commercial and military aircraft structures relied primarily on aluminum alloys due to their predictable isotropic properties and well-established fabrication methods. However, the pressing necessity to maximize fuel efficiency and payload capacity has propelled a comprehensive transition toward advanced composite materials, predominantly Carbon-Fiber-Reinforced Polymers, or CFRP. Unlike traditional metals, composite materials possess an anisotropic nature, meaning their mechanical strength and stiffness can be customized along specific load trajectories by orienting the carbon fibers during the manufacturing layup. This yields an exceptionally high strength-to-weight ratio. In state-of-the-art commercial jetliners, such as the Boeing 787 and Airbus A350, composites account for more than fifty percent of the total structural airframe weight. This substantial weight reduction decreases operating fuel consumption by approximately twenty percent compared to legacy aluminum airliners, while delivering superior resistance against environmental corrosion and fatigue cracking. Nevertheless, composite structures introduce distinct maintenance and reliability challenges. Specifically, low-velocity impacts—such as ground service collisions or runway debris strikes—can induce internal delamination, which is the internal separation of resin plies. Because this damage often leaves no visible indentation on the external surface, it is known as Barely Visible Impact Damage. To diagnose subsurface flaws without destructive disassembly, aerospace engineers integrate continuous Structural Health Monitoring systems. By embedding networks of piezoelectric sensors and fiber-optic Bragg gratings into the composite laminates, acoustic emissions and ultrasonic wave reflections are continuously monitored, alerting technicians to structural degradation before catastrophic failure occurs.

Mühendislik Sorunu (Delamination): Düşük hızlı çarpmalarda iç katmanların ayrılması; dıştan görünmeyen hasar (Barely Visible Impact Damage - BVID).
Çözüm (SHM): Kompozit içine gömülen piezoelektrik ve fiber-optik Bragg sensörleriyle Gerçek Zamanlı Yapısal Sağlık İzleme.

Instead of passively re-reading highlighting markers in textbooks, students should test themselves by attempting practice questions or summarizing concepts in their own words without looking at their notes. Incorporating twenty minutes of active recall every evening doubles long-term retention compared to passive reading.

Deontological frameworks posit that cognitive autonomy is the foundational prerequisite for moral agency; once external algorithmic entities possess real-time diagnostic surveillance over unconscious neural states, the very concept of voluntary consent becomes compromised. audio_script: In this advanced physics colloquium, we will analyze the disruptive vector posed by Shor's quantum algorithm against contemporary asymmetric cryptographic architectures. Current global banking, secure communications, and national defense protocols depend almost ubiquitously on the computational intractability of integer factorization, exemplified by RSA cryptosystems. A fault-tolerant quantum computer leveraging superposition and quantum phase estimation renders this polynomial-time reduction feasible, effectively obliterating the security assurances that underpin classical public-key cryptography. To counteract this existential cryptographic vulnerability, post-quantum cryptography has converged on lattice-based algebraic structures, such as learning-with-errors problems, which remain computationally intractable even for quantum adversaries utilizing Grover or Shor routines. Furthermore, quantum key distribution guarantees information-theoretic security rooted in the Heisenberg uncertainty principle and the no-cloning theorem, meaning any interception attempts introduce detectable quantum state collapses. Thus, the transition to post-quantum resilience is not merely a theoretical prerogative, but an immediate infrastructural imperative.

title: How Spaced Repetition Improves Language Memory

audio_script: Welcome everyone. In today's mini-lecture, we explore the science of spaced repetition. In the late nineteenth century, German psychologist Hermann Ebbinghaus discovered the forgetting curve. He proved that humans forget nearly fifty percent of newly learned information within twenty-four hours unless it is reviewed. Spaced repetition counteracts this by scheduling reviews at systematically increasing intervals—such as after one day, three days, one week, and one month. Using digital flashcards that employ spaced algorithms allows language students to transfer words from short-term memory into permanent long-term storage.

title: Understanding the Human Circadian Rhythm
subtitle: Koç Üniversitesi Sağlık Bilimleri Dersi
instructions_tr: Biyolojik saat ve uyku döngüsünü anlatan dersi dinleyin.
audio_script: Every human body possesses an internal biological clock known as the circadian rhythm. Regulated by a tiny cluster of cells in the brain called the suprachiasmatic nucleus, this 24-hour cycle governs sleepiness, core body temperature, and hormone production. When specialized photoreceptors in our retinas detect morning sunlight, the brain suppresses the sleep hormone melatonin, making us alert. Conversely, in the evening, darkness triggers melatonin synthesis, preparing the body for rest. Exposing eyes to bright blue light from smartphone screens before bed disrupts melatonin secretion, leading to chronic insomnia among students.

title: The Fundamentals of 3D Printing Technology

instructions_tr: 3D yazıcı teknolojisi ve eklemeli imalatı dinleyin.
audio_script: Three-dimensional printing, technically referred to as additive manufacturing, creates physical objects directly from digital computer-aided design models. Unlike traditional subtractive manufacturing—which cuts or carves material away from a solid block—a 3D printer deposits successive layers of plastic, resin, or metal powder on top of each other until the object is complete. This layer-by-layer technique drastically minimizes raw material waste and allows engineers to fabricate complex internal geometries that are impossible with conventional molds. Today, 3D printing is utilized in aerospace engineering, custom medical prosthetics, and architectural modeling.

Conventional flood irrigation is notoriously wasteful, losing up to fifty percent of water to surface evaporation and runoff. Agronomical field trials in the Konya basin demonstrate that smart drip systems diminish total agricultural water consumption by thirty-five percent while increasing crop yield by twelve percent. title: The Mechanism of Antibiotics and Bacterial Resistance

instructions_tr: Antibiyotiklerin çalışma mekanizması ve direnç sorununu dinleyip soruları cevaplayınız.
audio_script: In nineteen twenty-eight, Alexander Fleming serendipitously discovered penicillin, inaugurating the antibiotic era. Antibiotics function by selectively attacking cellular components unique to bacteria that are absent in human mammalian cells. For instance, beta-lactam antibiotics inhibit the synthesis of peptidoglycan, the rigid structural molecule that forms bacterial cell walls. Without this protective wall, osmotic pressure causes the bacterial cell to burst and die. However, widespread overprescription of antibiotics in veterinary livestock and clinical medicine has accelerated antibacterial resistance. Through spontaneous genetic mutation and horizontal gene transfer via plasmids, resistant bacterial strains produce enzymes like beta-lactamases that neutralize medical drugs. The World Health Organization warns that superbugs could cause ten million annual fatalities by 2050 unless novel antimicrobial therapies are developed.

Deep subsurface reservoirs contain pressurized water superheated to over two hundred degrees Celsius by geothermal magma gradients. In binary-cycle power stations, this hydrothermal fluid is extracted through deep boreholes to vaporize a secondary working fluid with a lower boiling point, which drives electrical generation turbines. Crucially, contemporary environmental standards mandate complete closed-loop reinjection. Once the heat is extracted, the cooled mineralized brine must be pumped back into the subterranean reservoir to prevent surface river contamination and preserve aquifer pressure. Rather than attempting to crack complex cryptographic firewalls, malicious actors exploit human cognitive heuristics through deception. A typical spear-phishing email mimics an urgent communication from a university administrator or banking official, prompting the recipient to click a fraudulent hyperlink and input credentials. Robust organizational cybersecurity requires a multi-layered defense model. First, machine-learning email filters analyze sender domain signatures and quarantine suspicious attachments. Second, mandating multi-factor authentication ensures that stolen passwords alone are insufficient to compromise accounts. Finally, regular employee simulation drills build institutional vigilance against social manipulation.

audio_script: Good morning. In today's marine biology seminar, we examine the ecotoxicological dynamics of microplastics across aquatic food webs. Microplastics, defined as synthetic polymer fragments under five millimeters in diameter, originate from two primary sources: primary microbeads manufactured for industrial cosmetics, and secondary fragments generated via mechanical weathering and solar ultraviolet photolysis of discarded packaging. Once washed into marine environments, buoyant microplastics adsorb hydrophobic organic pollutants, such as polychlorinated biphenyls and DDT, from surrounding seawater at concentrations up to a million times higher than ambient levels. Filter-feeding zooplankton indiscriminately ingest these toxin-coated synthetic particles, mistakenly treating them as organic phytoplankton. As apex marine predators like tuna and swordfish consume thousands of contaminated prey species, chemical toxins bioaccumulate and biomagnify up the trophic pyramid, ultimately reaching human seafood consumers and inducing endocrine disruption.

title: Behavioral Economics and Choice Architecture
subtitle: Bilkent COPE Tarzı Note-Taking Sınavı
instructions_tr: Davranışsal iktisat ve 'Dürtme' (Nudge) teorisini dinleyerek not alınız.
audio_script: Traditional neoclassical economics rested upon the premise of Homo economicus—an idealized human agent possessing infinite cognitive capacity and relentless rationality. However, behavioral economists Richard Thaler and Cass Sunstein proved that human decision-making is systematically bounded by cognitive heuristics, emotional biases, and inertia. To improve social outcomes without coercive mandates, they formulated 'nudge theory' and choice architecture. A nudge alters the context in which individuals make choices without forbidding any options or altering economic incentives. For example, in organ donation policy, countries operating under opt-in systems—where citizens must actively sign a donor card—exhibit consent rates around fifteen percent. Conversely, in opt-out regimes, where citizens are automatically registered as organ donors unless they explicitly check a box to decline, consent rates exceed ninety percent. Simply altering the default choice leverages human status-quo inertia to save thousands of lives.

title: Quantum Computing: Superposition and Entanglement

instructions_tr: Kuantum bilgisayarların temel ilkelerini dinleyip soruları cevaplayınız.
audio_script: Classical digital computers store and process information in binary digits, or bits, which exist strictly in one of two deterministic states: zero or one. Quantum computers, by contrast, utilize quantum bits, or qubits, which harness the bizarre principles of quantum mechanics. The first fundamental principle is quantum superposition. Thanks to wave-particle duality, a qubit can exist in a linear combination of both zero and one simultaneously until a physical measurement collapses its wavefunction. This allows a quantum processor containing three hundred qubits to represent more computational states simultaneously than there are atoms in the observable universe. The second principle is quantum entanglement, an interconnected state where the measurement of one qubit instantaneously determines the state of its paired partner, regardless of physical separation. Together, superposition and entanglement enable quantum algorithms to solve complex molecular simulations and factor massive prime numbers exponentially faster than classical supercomputers.

audio_script: The urban heat island phenomenon occurs when metropolitan centers experience ambient air temperatures several degrees higher than surrounding rural peripheries. This thermal disparity stems from modern urban morphology: dark asphalt roadways and dense concrete structures possess high thermal mass and low albedo, absorbing solar radiation during peak daylight and reradiating sensible heat well into the night. Furthermore, tall skyscrapers create deep urban canyons that trap anthropogenic heat emitted by vehicular combustion and air conditioning units. Bioclimatic architects mitigate this thermal trap through passive environmental engineering. First, retrofitting building roofs with high-albedo cool paints and intensive vegetative green roofs reduces surface absorption and promotes evapotranspirative cooling. Second, designing municipal street orientations to align with prevailing sea breezes ventilates trapped pollutants, lowering city center temperatures by up to four degrees Celsius.

audio_script: As nations strive to decarbonize transportation, liquid biofuels have emerged as critical transition fuels. However, there is a fundamental technological and ethical division between first and second-generation biofuels. First-generation bioethanol is derived from edible food crops, such as sugarcane and corn, by fermenting simple starch sugars. While technologically straightforward, this sparked the 'food versus fuel' debate, as diverting arable farmland toward ethanol production precipitated global grain price inflation and deforestation. In contrast, second-generation advanced biofuels utilize non-food lignocellulosic biomass, including agricultural residues like wheat straw, corn husks, and dedicated energy grasses. Breaking down resilient lignocellulose requires complex enzymatic hydrolysis and specialized microbial fermentation, but it avoids competition with human food supplies while generating eighty percent fewer greenhouse emissions than petroleum.

audio_script: Good morning. Today we examine the epistemological crisis triggered by algorithmic information filtering in digital public spheres. Contemporary social media platforms operate upon surveillance capitalism business models: user attentional retention is the primary monetizable commodity. To maximize engagement metrics, recommendation algorithms prioritize content that triggers intense visceral arousal, particularly righteous moral indignation. When users interact with sensationalist partisan posts, the neural ranking system constructs an epistemological filter bubble. The algorithm systematically conceals nuanced moderate discourse while inundating the user with affirming ideological narratives. This generates epistemic echo chambers where confirmation bias operates unimpeded. Sociological studies at Harvard demonstrate that this algorithmic tribalism destroys the shared empirical baseline necessary for democratic deliberation. When citizens of a republic cannot agree upon verified scientific or historical facts, governance degenerates into affective polarization where opposing factions view each other not as political rivals, but as existential threats to the body politic.

title: Neuroplasticity and Synaptic Consolidation in Sleep
subtitle: Hacettepe Üniversitesi Nörobilim Dersi
instructions_tr: Nöroplastisite ve uykuda hafıza pekiştirme dersini dinleyip not alınız.
audio_script: For centuries, the human brain was conceptualized as a static, immutable anatomical apparatus once biological adulthood was reached. Modern neurobiology has demolished this dogma through the paradigm of neuroplasticity—the nervous system's capacity to structurally reorganize its architecture and synaptic connectivity in response to experiential learning. Long-term potentiation, or LTP, serves as the primary cellular mechanism underlying memory formation: repeated high-frequency stimulation between presynaptic and postsynaptic neurons strengthens dendritic receptor density. However, synaptic potentiation alone is insufficient for permanent knowledge retention; it requires sleep-dependent consolidation. During slow-wave non-REM sleep, the hippocampus acts as a temporary buffer, replaying newly acquired neuronal firing sequences to the neocortex via sharp-wave ripples. This active system consolidation permanently stabilizes fragile short-term memories into enduring cortical schemas. Concurrently, during REM sleep, synaptic pruning downscales redundant neural connections, optimizing metabolic efficiency and integrating abstract conceptual insights.

title: International Trade Law and Sovereign Debt Restructuring

audio_script: When sovereign nation-states encounter balance-of-payments crises and face fiscal insolvency, the international legal architecture lacks a statutory bankruptcy mechanism analogous to domestic corporate liquidation courts. Sovereign immunity shields state infrastructure from direct judicial asset seizure abroad. Consequently, sovereign debt restructuring relies heavily on decentralized contractual arrangements between debtor states and international bondholder cartels. A recurring legal obstacle is the 'holdout creditor' problem. Speculative hedge funds, termed vulture funds, purchase defaulted sovereign bonds on secondary markets at steep discounts, deliberately refusing to participate in negotiated debt haircuts. They then litigate in New York or London commercial courts, demanding one hundred percent face-value repayment plus accrued punitive interest. To neutralize predatory holdout litigation, contemporary sovereign bond indentures incorporate Collective Action Clauses (CACs). Under modern aggregation CACs, if a supermajority of creditors—typically seventy-five percent—approves a restructuring agreement, the modified financial terms become legally binding across all outstanding bondholders, preserving the sovereign debtor's fiscal solvency.

audio_script: Climate science increasingly focuses on nonlinear dynamics: critical thresholds where minor incremental shifts in atmospheric greenhouse concentrations precipitate irreversible, self-reinforcing biophysical transformations, known as tipping points. Among the most precarious systems is the polar cryosphere. The ice-albedo positive feedback loop illustrates this vulnerability. Bright sea ice reflects up to eighty-five percent of incoming solar radiation back into space. As rising global temperatures melt Arctic ice sheets, reflective white surfaces are replaced by dark ocean water, which absorbs over ninety percent of solar thermal energy. This accelerated oceanic heat absorption triggers further sea ice melting in an escalating spiral. Concurrently, warming Arctic temperatures destabilize sub-polar permafrost, unleashing vast subterranean reservoirs of sequestered methane gas. Because methane possesses a greenhouse warming potential approximately eighty times greater than carbon dioxide over a twenty-year horizon, permafrost thaw threatens to trigger runaway global warming that transcends human emissions mitigation.

Pioneered by synthetic biologist Craig Venter, researchers synthesized the complete bacterial genome of Mycoplasma mycoides chemically from raw nucleotides and transplanted it into anucleated recipient cells, generating viable synthetic organism capable of independent replication. Concurrently, Nobel laureate Frances Arnold developed the methodology of directed evolution, harnessing Darwinian natural selection in test tubes. By generating iterative rounds of random mutagenesis across targeted gene sequences and screening for optimal enzymatic phenotypes, directed evolution creates biocatalysts with unprecedented catalytic efficiency. These engineered enzymes synthesize complex pharmaceutical molecules without petroleum solvents, degrade non-biodegradable plastics in landfills, and optimize biohydrogen generation. However, dual-use biosecurity risks necessitate stringent genomic surveillance to prevent malicious synthesis of biological pathogens.

title: Constitutional Jurisprudence and the Counter-Majoritarian Dilemma

audio_script: In constitutional theory, judicial review refers to the institutional power of supreme or constitutional courts to invalidate legislative statutes enacted by elected parliaments if they violate fundamental constitutional protections. In nineteen sixty-two, legal scholar Alexander Bickel coined the phrase 'the counter-majoritarian difficulty' to encapsulate the core philosophical tension of judicial review: how can a constitutional democracy justify allowing a small panel of unelected, life-tenured judges to overturn laws passed by the democratically elected representatives of the popular majority? Defenders of constitutionalism, rooted in Ronald Dworkin’s rights-based jurisprudence, counter that authentic democracy is not crude majoritarian tyranny. True democratic legitimacy requires substantive preconditions: universal franchise, freedom of speech, and the protection of minority populations against majoritarian prejudice. When constitutional courts strike down discriminatory legislation, they are not thwarting democracy; they are upholding the fundamental constitutional integrity that makes democratic self-governance morally legitimate in the first place.

title: Epistemological Fallibilism and Underdetermination of Scientific Theory
subtitle: Boğaziçi BUEPT Doktora & İleri C2 Note-Taking
instructions_tr: Bilim felsefesi ve Quine-Duhem tezini dinleyiniz. Dinlerken notlarınızı dijital deftere kaydediniz; ardından soruları yanıtlayınız.
audio_script: In the philosophy of science, the Duhem-Quine thesis articulates the holist underdetermination of scientific theory by empirical evidence. Classical logical positivism presupposed that individual scientific hypotheses could be subjected to isolated experimental verification or Popperian falsification. Willard Van Orman Quine decisively undermined this atomistic reductionism by asserting that our knowledge of the world faces the tribunal of experience not as disconnected propositions, but as an interconnected web of belief. When an empirical observation contradicts a theoretical prediction, logic alone cannot specify which particular thread within the theoretical fabric is falsified. A recalcitrant observation can always be accommodated by introducing auxiliary hypotheses, re-calibrating observational instruments, or revising background assumptions. Consequently, multiple rival theoretical paradigms can remain logically compatible with identical empirical data sets. Scientific realism must therefore embrace fallibilism: recognizing that empirical paradigms are underdetermined heuristic models rather than mirror reflections of metaphysical reality.

title: Posthumanism, Cyborg Ontology, and the Dissolution of Liberal Humanism

audio_script: Critical posthumanism mounts an ontological deconstruction of the Enlightenment humanist subject—the sovereign, rational, autonomous individual historically constructed through patriarchal, colonial, and anthropocentric exclusions. As cultural theorist Donna Haraway demonstrated in her seminal Cyborg Manifesto, technological interfaces have irreversibly collapsed the foundational dualisms underpinning Western metaphysics: the ontological boundaries between nature and culture, organism and mechanism, human and animal. The cyborg figure is not a dystopic alienation from an Edenic natural origin, but an affirmation of hybridity, relationality, and leaky boundaries. In the contemporary Anthropocene, human survival necessitates abandoning the illusion of sovereign planetary mastery. A relational posthumanist ethics demands acknowledging non-human agency and technological imbrication, recognizing that human subjectivity is fundamentally distributed across ecological webs, algorithmic neural networks, and biological symbiogeneses.

Their diagnosis centered upon the catastrophic degeneration of subjective reason into pure instrumental rationality. The Enlightenment promised emancipation from myth and theological superstition through scientific understanding. However, in subduing external nature, reason was stripped of its capacity to evaluate objective moral ends, values, and human justice. Instrumental reason became an operational calculating technique dedicated solely to utilitarian mastery, technical efficiency, and commodity exchange. Consequently, nature—and ultimately human beings themselves—were reduced to quantifiable, manipulable objects of administrative control. When reason is reduced to a tool of domination, bureaucratic efficiency culminates not in human liberation, but in totalitarian administration and industrial mass destruction.

title: Biosemiotics and Jakob von Uexküll's Umwelt Theory
subtitle: Sabancı Üniversitesi Biyosemiyotik Dersi
instructions_tr: Biyosemiyotik ve canlıların algısal dünyalarını (Umwelt) anlatan dersi dinleyiniz.
audio_script: Biosemiotics bridges theoretical biology and semiotics by positing that life is fundamentally mediated through sign processes and meaning-making, or semiosis. Early twentieth-century theoretical biologist Jakob von Uexküll overthrew mechanistic behaviorism by introducing the concept of the 'Umwelt'—the subjective perceptual bubble unique to every organism. Mechanistic science assumes an objective, universal physical environment, or 'Umgebung', identical for all creatures. Uexküll proved that an organism does not interact with the entirety of physical reality, but only with those environmental cues for which its specialized sensory receptors, or 'Merkorgane', are physiologically tuned. For a blind tick, the world consists of only three operational carrier signs: the scent of butyric acid, the thermal heat of mammalian blood, and the hairiness of skin. All other physical stimuli—colors, symphonies, chemical pollutants—are non-existent within its phenomenological reality. Thus, nature is not a monolithic physical mechanism, but a vast, polyphonic polyphony of interlocking perceptual Umwelten.

title: Systemic Risk, Network Topology, and Financial Contagion
subtitle: Koç Üniversitesi İleri Ekonometri ve Finans Semineri
instructions_tr: Finansal ağ topolojisi ve sistemik çöküş modellemelerini dinleyiniz.
audio_script: The two-thousand-eight global financial collapse decisively demonstrated that systemic risk cannot be appraised by evaluating individual financial institutions in micro-prudential isolation. Modern macroprudential econometrics models financial stability through complex network topology. Financial systems are structured as directed, weighted graphs where nodes represent banking institutions and edges denote interbank obligations, derivative exposures, and collateralized debt cross-holdings. In quiescent economic periods, dense interconnectedness enhances financial resilience by dissipating localized liquidity shocks across the entire network. However, network theorists Andrew Haldane and Robert May revealed a non-linear tipping point: when shocks exceed a critical threshold, dense topological interconnectedness transforms into a hyper-efficient conduit for financial contagion. As distressed institutions liquidate illiquid assets in fire sales, asset depreciation cascades through counterparty balance sheets, triggering systemic insolvency. Effective macroprudential regulation requires identifying systemic topologically central nodes and enforcing countercyclical capital buffers.

- Sakin dönemde yoğun bağlantılılık yerel şokları dağıtarak direnç sağlar
- Kriz anında ise sistemik bulaşma (contagion) kanalına dönüşür
Mekanizma: Varlık yangın satışı (fire sale) -> Bilanço erimesi -> Zincirleme iflas
Çözüm: Ağın merkezindeki kritik düğümlere döngü karşıtı sermaye tamponu (countercyclical buffer) zorunluluğu

title: Necropolitics, Sovereignty, and Spaces of Exception in Border Regimes
subtitle: Ankara Üniversitesi Siyaset Felsefesi Dersi
instructions_tr: Nekropolitika ve egemen istisna halleri üzerine felsefi dersi dinleyin.
audio_script: Achille Mbembe’s seminal paradigm of 'necropolitics' reformulates classical theories of sovereignty by positing that ultimate sovereign power resides not in the management and optimization of biological life—as Michel Foucault argued in his biopolitical lectures—but in the sovereign prerogative to dictate who is disposable and who may be exposed to death. Synthesizing Giorgio Agamben’s concept of the 'state of exception' with postcolonial critique, Mbembe demonstrates that modern sovereignty materializes most tangibly in geographical border regimes. Frontiers, offshore detention centers, and militarized maritime boundaries operate as contemporary spaces of exception where constitutional guarantees and international humanitarian law are suspended through administrative decree. Within these necropolitical zones, stateless refugees are stripped of political existence, reduced to what Agamben termed 'bare life'—human existence devoid of juridical rights. By weaponizing hostile geography—forcing migrants into treacherous desert expanses or unnavigable maritime channels—the sovereign state manufactures conditions of mass mortality while preserving formal legal deniability.

title: Thermodynamic Entropy, Information Theory, and Cosmological Arrows of Time
subtitle: İTÜ Teorik Fizik ve Kozmoloji Semineri
instructions_tr: Termodinamik entropi, bilgi teorisi ve zamanın oku dersini dinleyin.
audio_script: The macroscopic unidirectionality of time represents one of the most enigmatic conundrums in fundamental physics. While the microscopic laws of classical mechanics, quantum wavefunctions, and general relativity are strictly time-reversal symmetric, human macroscopic reality exhibits an immutable chronological arrow pointing inexorably from past to future. The second law of thermodynamics grounds this asymmetry in statistical entropy: the spontaneous evolution of isolated thermodynamic systems from macrostates of low multiplicity to macrostates of overwhelmingly higher probability. In the nineteen forties, Claude Shannon formulated mathematical information theory, proving that thermodynamic entropy is mathematically isomorphic to information entropy: entropy quantifies the missing microscopic information required to specify a physical microstate given macroscopic thermodynamic coordinates. To account for why our present universe has not already reached thermal equilibrium or 'heat death', cosmologists postulate the Past Hypothesis: our universe originated in an extraordinarily low-entropy gravitational boundary condition at the Big Bang, establishing the thermodynamic reservoir from which all cosmic complexity and subjective time flow.

title: Structural Semiotics and Derrida's Différance
subtitle: Genel C2 İleri Felsefe ve Dilbilim
instructions_tr: Jacques Derrida'nın yapısöküm (deconstruction) ve différance kavramını dinleyip soruları yanıtlayın.
audio_script: In twentieth-century continental philosophy, Jacques Derrida's deconstructive intervention radicalized Saussurean structural linguistics by interrogating the Western metaphysical tradition of the 'metaphysics of presence'. Ferdinand de Saussure had demonstrated that language is a system of differential signs without positive terms: a signifier signifies only by virtue of what it is not within a relational network. Derrida observed that Western philosophy had persistently repressed this differential nature by seeking an ultimate 'transcendental signified'—an unmediated, self-present origin such as God, Reason, or Sensory Immediacy. To deconstruct this illusion, Derrida coined the neologism 'différance', combining the dual French meanings of differing and deferring. Meaning, Derrida asserts, is never fully present in a discrete linguistic sign; it is spatially differentiated from other signifiers and temporally deferred across an infinite chain of sign substitution. Because meaning is perpetually postponed, all texts contain unresolvable internal contradictions, or aporias, that systematically undo their own totalizing claims.
